biography: James Jackson, a name whispered with a mix of awe and apprehension in the junior racing circuits, hails from the small Norwegian town of Ålesund. Born to a family with no motorsport background, James's passion ignited after witnessing a rally race as a child. He started karting at the age of 12, quickly outgrowing the local scene with his raw talent and fearless driving style. A defining moment came at the Norwegian Junior Karting Championship in 2021, where, despite starting last due to a technical issue, he stormed through the field to clinch victory on the final lap, showcasing his relentless spirit. Now at 17, James is making waves in the Formula Nordic series, running as an independent driver, relying on sheer grit and determination to compete against teams with far greater resources. He's a long shot, but many see a diamond in the rough.
drivingStyle: James's driving style is best described as controlled aggression. He's known for his late braking maneuvers and willingness to take risks in corners, often pushing the limits of grip to gain an advantage. While his tire management skills are still developing, his raw speed and ability to extract every ounce of performance from his machinery make him a formidable competitor. He thrives under pressure, often delivering his best performances in high-stakes situations, showcasing a remarkable composure for his age.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky socks, regardless of weather.
Listens to a specific obscure Norwegian folk song before every race.
Refuses to walk under ladders, even in the paddock.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2021 Norwegian Junior Karting Championship from last place after a dramatic final lap overtake.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final race of the 2023 Formula Nordic season due to a mechanical failure, costing him the championship.
